title: Visual and Functional Testing
keywords: accessibility, performance, debugging, and professional practice
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of visual and functional testing and when it is appropriate.
Apply page-level layout checks using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check form validation tests and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study visual and functional testing and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Visual and Functional Testing makes the interface more robust for real users and real content. Measure and reproduce behavior, inspect semantics and focus, and document the browser, viewport, steps, and result so another developer can repeat the check.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Visual and Functional Testing makes the interface more robust for real users and real content. Measure and reproduce behavior, inspect semantics and focus, and document the browser, viewport, steps, and result so another developer can repeat the check.

content_blocks.code: Use a layered test plan: static markup checks, browser interaction checks, responsive manual tests, automated regression where available, and accessibility review.
content_blocks.expected_output: The example illustrates visual and functional testing. Expected review result: static-validation can be followed and the intended behavior or configuration can be explained; the lesson-specific acceptance checks still apply.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, undo one change at a time, and repeat the same browser/build check. Do not keep temporary debugging rules in the final implementation.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.x baseline, follow the official component documentation, and verify semantic HTML, responsive behavior, and keyboard access before reusing the pattern.

content.task: Run a structured review centered on visual and functional testing. Record reproducible steps, expected versus actual behavior, and one next fix or acceptance test.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the purpose and appropriate use of visual and functional testing.
Use the documented class, component, API, or workflow correctly.
Record a responsive, accessibility, or build verification relevant to this example.
hints: Start with the smallest source example in this lesson.
Change one class, attribute, or configuration item at a time.
Compare expected behavior with the result; consult the linked official page if the version-specific behavior differs.
content.expected_output: A working or reviewed example of visual and functional testing, with a short explanation and recorded verification steps.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating visual and functional testing as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
